chapter: Rhythm and blues, the Howard Theatre and later years
title: Al Dunn's Music Hall house band, then a government job from 1956
summary: Phillips recalls the 1947 house band at the Music Hall opening with Louis Armstrong, then Albert Curtis's band until he took a government job in 1956 and retired in 1971.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Then after that, Al Dunn got a band together, and went up to the Music Hall. Stayed up there about four months. We was the house band there. We opened up with Louis Armstrong's band. Lionel Hampton stayed up there two weeks. Tony Pastor. Cootie Williams. Jimmy Lunceford...
This was a little earlier. I thought you were talking about '54. You played with All Dunn in '47?
Yeah. Then comin' on down to '54, Albert Curtis... I played with him until I got a job in the government. That was in '56. That's when I went into the government, in '56.
You worked with the government how long?
18 years would have been '74. Anyway, you retired in '71?
